name: avatar_bff
title: trust-chain.ai Avatar BFF: the owner lane between a local apatch and HC Tracker

provider.note: The host is shared with TrustChain Platform. nginx routes /api/pub, /api/log, /api/enroll, /api/org, /api/licenses, /api/agents, /api/tenants, /api/ca, /api/owner, /api/embed-integrations to the Platform; every other /api/* path, /api/avatar included, reaches the Agent.

auth.apatch: Authorization: Bearer <tcav_...> — a revocable owner-scoped Avatar sync token minted on Avatar Home; accepted only by routes marked consumer=apatch

identity_gate.detail: the refusing status is the response body's detail, verbatim
identity_gate.notes: The BFF resolves the caller's HC professional on every owner operation; an earlier success never authorizes a later request. When the owner is not resolved, gated_routes refuse with the HTTP code above and answering_routes still answer 200 with available=false and the same status. A 409 says the person must connect or reactivate their HC profile: it is not retryable on its own, so a consumer stops the lane, keeps its outbox intact and reports the detail. A 503 is retryable.

success.notes: decisions[] are TaxonomyDecision wires whose subject_avatar_id equals avatar_id; apatch verifies each against its pinned issuer keys

rules: every event has source=apatch, event_id, idempotency_key, signature and proof_ref (or legacy attestation)
one batch belongs to exactly one principal key_id

success.notes: failed[] items are {event_id, status}; a status in permanent_rejection_statuses quarantines the event locally, anything else is retried
present/missing/conflict are a disjoint exact partition of the requested ids; if either verified key is present both must be and together they partition present_event_ids

not_ready.notes: identity_unbound when avatar_id is not in the authenticated owner's portfolio

request.evidence: CapabilityEvidence v2 bundle (kind=capability_evidence, source=apatch, bundle_id, avatar_id == signature.key_id)

success.notes: apatch acknowledges only status_code 200 AND accepted=true AND signature_verified=true

not_ready.notes: hc_identity_unbound carries connect_url so the client can start the HC SSO binding (SPEC-HC-SSO-BINDING-1); identity_unbound means the HC professional has no principal key yet

request.counterparty_company_id: the contract counterparty that received the work (ADR-SEC-018 invariant 2)

errors.409: review_conflict, or an identity_gate status when the caller's HC profile is not connected or not active
errors.503: tracker unavailable or misconfigured, or an identity_gate status

errors.409: review_conflict, or an identity_gate status when the caller's HC profile is not connected or not active

success.notes: token is the raw tcav_ secret shown exactly once; sync_token is the stored record (id, label, token_hint, created_at, expires_at, last_used_at, revoked_at); issuing a replacement revokes every earlier active token of the owner

status_notes.tracker_rejected: as a whole-response status it is a not-ready outcome (retry later); as a per-event failed[].status it is permanent and the event is quarantined locally
status_notes.partial_failure: contributions.upload answers available=false with status=partial_failure; consumers key on status and on failed[], not on available
status_notes.owner_lane_literal_sequence: apatch's literal call order is taxonomy, outcomes, reconcile, upload, reconcile, evidence: reconciliation brackets the upload; owner_lane_order lists the order in which each step settles
status_notes.hc_identity_inactive: the SSO subject is bound to an HC professional the HC identity directory reports as not active; on gated_routes it is refused like hc_identity_unbound, with 409
status_notes.review_409_is_ambiguous: on outcome_reviews.create and outcome_reviews.resubmit a 409 is review_conflict OR an identity_gate status; the client reads detail, never the code alone
